newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, Russia hold talks over Turkish incursion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Russia hold talks over Turkish incursion.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz on Wednesday discussed with a Russian envoy the Turkish incursion into northern Iraq and U.N. trade sanctions on Baghdad, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

INA said Aziz met the visiting head of Russian foreign ministry's Middle East department Andrei Vdovin to follow up the outcome of Aziz's meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeni Primakov in Moscow earlier this month.
It said Aziz discussed with Vdoviv "means of lifting the unjust embargo and the Turkish invasion of Iraqi territory".
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq earlier this month in pursuit of separatist guerrillas of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
Aziz accused the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday of being "indifferent" to the Turkish incursion.
The Iraqi deputy premier was in Moscow in early May to seek Russia's help in having the U.N. sanctions, imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, removed.
Moscow wants an immediate lifting of the sanctions to revive its once lucrative trade with Baghdad.
Iraq signed a multi-billion oil deal with Russia in March allowing Russian firms to develop seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in Iraq's southern Qurana oilfield.
